It differs from standard SVO ray tracing by storing per-voxel optical properties (IOR, reflectivity) to enable heterogeneous refraction, where light rays are re-bent at every voxel boundary with a different index of refraction, rather than treating the volume as a homogeneous medium or refracting only at the surface [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from standard SVO ray tracing by storing per-voxel optical properties (IOR, reflectivity) to enable heterogeneous refraction, where light rays are re-bent at every voxel boundary with a different index of refraction. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the passage: 'As well as a colour and a normal, each voxel stores how reflective it is and its index of refraction... When a ray goes into something see-through, it's bent using Snell's law, and then stepped through the volume. Every time it moves into a voxel with a different index of refraction it gets bent again, so light can refract through an object that changes inside... not just off the outside of it.' This matches the claim's description of storing per-voxel properties and re-bending rays at boundaries with different IORs.
